header: QUESTIONS ABOUT THE FIRST DIGITS OF EXECUTIVES' CUG MOBILE NUMBERS ("find the executives whose CUG mobile number does not start with 943479"). My rule (23 Nov 2026): any signed-in executive may ask. Why this is not the AI's job: I never give the language model that writes the database questions any phone numbers, only a yes/no flag (src/lib/nl2sql/sql/01_nlq_schema_views_role.sql), so it must refuse such a question, and it does. The digits are tested HERE, by the application's own connection, in plain code: the sentence is read by rules (no model, no wait), the database is asked one question, and the answer is a list of people whose numbers stay MASKED on their cards (the Reveal button keeps its login check, its audit row and its hourly cap). What it takes, and what it refuses (so that it cannot become a way round the Reveal cap):

- "starts with" / "begins with" / "series" / "prefix", and the same with a "not": the first 1 to 6 digits. The first six digits of a CUG number are the series every executive shares (the six that follow the plant's own); I never allow the last four, which tell people apart, to be asked.

- "ends with", "contains", "last 4 digits", and a pattern of more than 6 digits are answered with a sentence that says they cannot be asked, and why: a prefix and a suffix together would rebuild a whole number.
- Only a signed-in executive (ticket 4xxxxx, the LOGIN's ticket) is answered; everybody else gets one sentence and the database is not asked.
- At most PER_HOUR questions an hour for one ticket (coarse: kept in this server copy's memory).
Pure apart from the `search` it is given. Tested by cugPattern.selftest.ts.

behaviours: the owner's sentence, typo and all ('does not starts with')
negation is read from the words BEFORE the digits only ('starts with 943479, not 94')
a pattern of more than 6 digits is refused as too long, not read
'ends with' and 'last 4 digits' are refused with their own reason
'contains' is refused with its own reason
a prefix together with a suffix is refused (the two would rebuild a number)
not ours: ${q}
an empty or an enormous line is not ours
nobody signed in: one sentence, and the database is not asked
a signed-in person who is not an executive (ticket not 4xxxxx) is refused the same way, nothing read
an executive asking for the END of a number is told why not, nothing read
a line that is not about the digits is left to the other routes (null)
an executive gets the list: the count, the people, the numbers masked on the cards (no e-mail carried)
the sentence says how many of how many, the rule, the 21 with no number, and that the numbers are masked
the interpretation names the rule in words, for the 'Understood as' line
no match: said plainly, not an empty list
a long list says it is cut, and shows the first hundred
singular and plural are right ('1 executive has no CUG number ... is not counted')
the ${PER_HOUR + 1}th question in an hour is refused and does not read the database
the allowance is per ticket
the step runs early in the engine, before the PAX and the model, for Everything and People only
the digits are read by the application's own connection (getDb) and tested in code; the model's views are untouched (still booleans only)
the digits limit and the allowance are the stated ones (6 digits, 30 an hour)
